ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached diagram shows a rectangular grid made of 4 columns and 2 rows of unit squares. The point labeled "Start" is at the upper-left corner of the rectangle, and the point labeled "Ziel" is at the lower-right corner. The allowed paths run along square sides and square diagonals. Reasoning: Model the diagram as a weighted grid graph. Assign coordinates Start = (0,0) and Ziel = (4,2), with x increasing to the right and y increasing downward. A side move has length 1, and a diagonal of a unit square has length sqrt(2). Since any move leftward or upward would have to be compensated later and would only add positive length, it is enough to consider monotone moves: right, down, and down-right diagonal. Let D(x,y) be the shortest remaining distance from vertex (x,y) to (4,2). Then D(x,y) = min(1 + D(x+1,y), 1 + D(x,y+1), sqrt(2) + D(x+1,y+1)), using only moves that stay inside the 4 by 2 grid, with D(4,2)=0. Filling from the target backward gives, for example: along the bottom row D(3,2)=1, D(2,2)=2, D(1,2)=3, D(0,2)=4; along the right edge D(4,1)=1, D(4,0)=2. The interior values then yield D(3,1)=sqrt(2), D(2,1)=1+sqrt(2), D(1,1)=2+sqrt(2), and finally D(0,0)=2+2sqrt(2). This corresponds to using two unit side moves and two unit-square diagonal moves.

From the text, a horizontal or vertical side move costs 1 and changes one coordinate by 1, while a down-right diagonal costs sqrt(2) and simultaneously supplies one rightward unit and one downward unit.
